takeaways.t: **The White House said on 13 Nov that President Trump will meet Presidents Putin and Xi in Shenzhen on Thursday 19 Nov, the first three-way meeting of the three leaders,** on the margins of the APEC summit, with nuclear arms reduction on the agenda. [9]

**EU leaders agreed in Dublin on 13 Nov that Europe's team for the Ukraine talks is the EU institutions and the E5: France, Germany, the UK, Italy and Poland;** Chancellor Merz said talks with Europe represented are expected “in the coming weeks”. [10, 11, 12]

**President Zelensky said on 13 Nov that Ukraine hopes for a prisoner exchange of more than 1,000 people on each side;** overnight Russia launched 117 drones, of which 80 were downed or suppressed. [13, 14]

**The Army on 13 Nov named Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner, assigned to NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks, as the officer held in Britain under the National Security Act 2023;** the same evening suspected drones set off sirens at RAF Lakenheath and Feltwell. [15, 16]

**Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on 13 Nov that a liquefied gas carrier caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz,** and that it had “targeted and destroyed” a US early-warning radar in Bahrain; no US or Bahraini response was published. [17, 18]

**Dutch coalition talks ended after more than eight hours on 13 Nov without a deal, and VVD leader Yeşilgöz called the minority cabinet a “mislukt experiment” (“failed experiment”);** the D66, VVD and CDA leaders resume today at De Zwaluwenberg. [5, 19]

items.h: Trump to meet Putin and Xi in Shenzhen on Thursday, the first three-way talk
items.body: The White House told reporters on 13 Nov that President Donald Trump will meet President Vladimir Putin and President Xi Jinping in China on Thursday 19 Nov, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen; it is the first time the three leaders meet in a three-way format. [9] The talks will cover reducing nuclear weapons; spokesperson Olivia Wales said, as NOS rendered it, “President Trump is van mening dat de uitbreiding van kernwapens zeer gevaarlijk is” (“President Trump believes the expansion of nuclear weapons is very dangerous”). [9] The last US–Russian nuclear arms treaty expired in February. [9] An unnamed US official told Reuters that Iran will be on the table and Ukraine will not; no one-to-one meeting between Trump and Putin is planned. [9]
items.next: Trump leaves Monday 16 Nov on a four-day trip to Asia that includes the Philippines; the two-day APEC summit opens on Wednesday 18 Nov and the three-way meeting is on 19 Nov. [9]

items.h: EU leaders name the EU institutions and five states as Europe's team for Ukraine talks
items.body: EU leaders agreed at an informal European Council in Dublin on 13 Nov that “the European team for the negotiations on peace in Ukraine is the European Union institutions and the E5 (countries) of the Coalition of the Willing,” Council President António Costa said. [10] EUobserver named the five as France, Germany, the UK, Italy and Poland, with no single envoy. [11] Costa added: “Only Ukraine has the legitimacy to decide on matters concerning its territory and sovereignty.” [10] Chancellor Friedrich Merz said: “In the coming weeks, concrete peace talks are expected to take place for the first time with Europe represented.” [12] Jared Kushner wrote on X on 12 Nov: “Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners.” [20]
items.next: No date or venue for the next round is published; Kushner said the schedule would be announced “shortly”. [20] The Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin on 19 Nov and the European Council on 26–27 Nov. [10, 21]

items.h: Zelensky says Ukraine hopes to swap more than 1,000 prisoners on each side
items.body: President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his evening address on 13 Nov: “We count on a truly large-scale prisoner exchange,” one that could see more than 1,000 people released on each side. [13] Kushner said the US is working toward the largest exchange of the war, a result of the Abu Dhabi talks on 10–11 Nov. [20] Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 117 strike drones, 63 of them jet-powered, overnight into 13 Nov; 80 were downed or suppressed, with hits at 24 locations. [14] A jet-powered Geran-5 was downed over the Kyiv region with a Swedish RBS-70 for the first time. [22] Ukrinform counted 243 clashes on 13 Nov, nearly 50 of them in the Pokrovsk sector, and a strike on Zaporizhzhia injured 50 people, eight of them children. [23, 24]
items.next: Zelensky said he expects a detailed briefing on the exchange preparations soon; no date is published. [13]

items.h: Revolutionary Guard says a gas carrier hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
items.body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on 13 Nov that a liquefied gas carrier caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, after it “ignored warnings and attempted to navigate an unauthorised route”. [17] The same day it said its forces “targeted and destroyed” a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, which IRNA said was hit by an “enemy” strike on the evening of 12 Nov. [18] The IRGC said that if such acts recur its Aerospace Force “stands in full readiness to engage without limits.” [18] No US or Bahraini response and no independent confirmation was published. [18] A UN assistant secretary-general called on 14 Nov for safe navigation to be restored in Hormuz and the Red Sea. [25]
items.next: No date is published for further contacts between Iran and the US.

items.h: EU and UK warn Kosovo MPs against curbing the Hague court's powers
items.body: The EU Office in Kosovo and the British Embassy in Pristina warned MPs on 13 Nov against passing amendments that curb the Kosovo Specialist Chambers' powers; the EU called for “prior consultations before any adoption, in line with Kosovo's international obligations.” [26] PDK MP Blerta Deliu-Kodra said on 12 Nov: “we have agreed to pass the bill, but there is no consensus on amending it.” [26] MPs first voted for the amended law on 6 Oct. [26]
items.next: No date for the final vote is published. [26]

feature.title: Eastern Congo's road war: the FRN pushes up national road 3 from Kalehe
body: The front that moved this week in eastern Congo runs along one road. National road 3 (RN3) leaves Bukavu on Lake Kivu and climbs west through Kahuzi-Biega National Park towards Walikale and, eventually, Kisangani. [27, 28] The FRN, the movement led by former president Joseph Kabila and launched in Goma on 12 Oct, took over from the AFC, the political wing of M23, whose commanders still lead on the ground. [27]

Its offensive began overnight on 6–7 Nov through the park and along RN3. [27, 28] By 8 Nov it held Bitale, Bulambika and Bunyakiri in Kalehe territory; Bulambika, about 30 km from Hombo on the Kalehe–Walikale border, has a general hospital, a health-zone office and a prison. [28, 29] Local civil society estimated that the FRN took 20 to 60 km of the road in two days, and a government counterattack on Kambale failed on 10 Nov. [28] The army's 34th military region said on 9 Nov: “Nous avons fixé l'ennemi. Il est stoppé au niveau de Bulambika.” (“We have pinned the enemy down. He is stopped at Bulambika.”) [27]

A preliminary humanitarian alert of 9 Nov counts 166,500 newly displaced people, about 27,750 households; the territory administrator put it at more than 160,000. [27, 30] Kinshasa accuses Kabila of acting for Rwanda, which Kigali denies. [27] Further north, the airport at Bunia in Ituri stays closed to all but humanitarian, medical and emergency flights to at least 8 Feb 2027 because of the Ebola outbreak declared there on 15 May. [31] Straight-line distances show the scale: Bukavu to Walikale is 151 km, Bukavu to Goma 101 km, and Goma to Bunia 379 km.

incidents.text: Sirens sounded at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk and RAF Feltwell in Norfolk at about 17:30 on 13 Nov; the US Air Force said the alarm was linked to “suspected unauthorized drones” and that no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected. [16] The UK Ministry of Defence said the situation was resolved; no operator was named. [32]

A phoned bomb threat led to the evacuation of 2,150 pupils and staff; federal police found nothing and released the building at 13:35. Police arrested a 17-year-old from Mechelen at 14:30 and placed him at the prosecutor's disposal. The same school was evacuated after a threat in early October, and authorities are checking whether the cases link. [33]

leads.title: Suspected drones set off sirens at RAF Lakenheath and Feltwell as the US raises base security in England
leads.teaser: The alarm came days after tankers left RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-related threat, and the same week the Army named an officer held in Britain.

RAF Lakenheath (Suffolk) and RAF Feltwell (Norfolk), evening of 13 Nov; about 125 km north-east of London. [16]
None. No operator was named, and no device was reported recovered. [16, 32]

A US European Command spokesperson said: “We continue to work closely with our host nation counterparts to ensure the safety and security of our US service members.” [16] The War Zone, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported FPCON Charlie at Mildenhall and Lakenheath over an Iranian threat, and that KC-135 tankers left Mildenhall from 9 Nov. [34]
The UK Ministry of Defence said it is working with the US to establish the facts; no date is given. [34]
leads.sw: Host-nation support: drone alarms over US bases in a NATO host nation test the civil-military arrangements for base protection and airfield use that reinforcement through Britain relies on, baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation).

**Drones:** Unauthorised drone activity over RAF Lakenheath on 13 Nov, single-source and resolved. [32]

**Infrastructure:** the US Federal Aviation Administration halted all US air traffic for about five hours on the night of 13–14 Nov after air-traffic-control communications equipment was overloaded; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed a large volume of data, not an attack. [35]
**Advisories:** NCSC-NL issued two advisories on 13 Nov (Ivanti Endpoint Manager, Zoom Workplace). [36]

europe.h: De Wever holds weekend budget talks before reporting to the King on Monday
europe.body: Prime Minister Bart De Wever called majority leaders to talks all weekend, with a core meeting at 19:00 on Friday 13 Nov, RTBF reported. [7] He wants a budget to 2029 with at least €10 billion in savings; without a deal a temporary budget applies from January. [7] He reports to the King on Monday 16 Nov at 10:30, and cancelled his trip to the Dublin summit. [7]
europe.sw: A caretaker Belgian government would slow decisions on host-nation support and defence spending for SHAPE and the NATO headquarters in the country.
europe.fy: Hold off on any Belgian official engagement that needs a budget decision until after the 16 Nov report.

europe.h: Security guarantees for Ukraine go to the Coalition of the Willing, coordinated with NATO
europe.body: At the informal Dublin summit on 13 Nov, EU leaders agreed that security guarantees for Ukraine sit with the Coalition of the Willing, coordinated with NATO, with no timeline given, EUobserver reported. [11] Whether High Representative Kaja Kallas gets a seat at the talks is unresolved; one senior diplomat said it was “just not possible”, and Kallas warned Russia was “setting traps” with a debate on NATO's role. [11] The Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin on 19 Nov. [21]
europe.sw: Guarantees coordinated with NATO set the planning frame for any post-ceasefire civil-military tasks, which is where JFC Brunssum's J9 would meet baseline requirement 1 (continuity of government) in Ukraine.

countries.h: Hungary pays over 6 billion forints seized in the Seszták case into the Treasury
countries.body: Hungary's asset recovery office (NVVH) said on 13 Nov that searches on 12 and 13 Nov in Budapest and Pest, Békés and Nógrád counties found cash tied to the criminal case against former minister Miklós Seszták (KDNP). [38] The haul was 5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100, reportedly buried in forests and hidden in farm buildings and a safe. [38] Seszták has been in custody since 28 Sep on suspicion of taking 12.6 billion forints in bribes in a Volánbusz case; these are allegations, not a verdict. [38] Interfax put the seizure at about €17.7 million on 14 Nov. [39] Finance Minister András Kármán said 12 Treasury staff spent eight hours counting the cash with five machines. [38]
countries.sw: Budget line: Hungary's civil-resilience spending leans on the EU money held back over rule-of-law conditions, so visible asset recovery bears on the hu-eu-funds indicator and on baseline requirement 1 (continuity of government).

q.t: A hatóság közlése szerint a teljes összeget pénteken befizették a Magyar Államkincstárba.
q.en: According to the authority, the full amount was paid into the Hungarian State Treasury on Friday.

countries.h: EPPO closes its case over Slovakia's 2022 ammunition donation to Ukraine
countries.body: The European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) stopped its investigation into suspected misuse of European Peace Facility funds for ammunition Slovakia sent to Ukraine in 2022, TASR reported on 13 Nov. [40] The case, opened in April 2025, ended because “zabezpečené dôkazy nepreukázali spáchanie trestného činu” (“the evidence secured did not prove a criminal offence”). [40] EPPO found the ministry used the urgency exception in procurement law, all ammunition was delivered and the price matched the market. [40] In June 2025 EPPO had reported a suspected €7.4 million embezzlement and eight detentions. [40]
countries.sw: Budget line: the case concerned European Peace Facility money and the security-urgency exemption that direct-award buys of allied ammunition rely on, so the closure bears on how freely Slovak procurement can use that route.

q.t: zabezpečené dôkazy nepreukázali spáchanie trestného činu
q.en: the evidence secured did not prove a criminal offence

countries.h: Bild reports Russian terms that would bar NATO bases in the Baltic states
countries.body: Index reported on 13 Nov, citing the German paper Bild, that an unofficial Russian proposal shown to European representatives at the Abu Dhabi talks would demand “az európai biztonsági rendszer átalakítását” (“a transformation of the European security system”) in exchange for ending the war. [41] It would block further NATO enlargement, bar NATO bases in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania and have Finland leave NATO, while Russia would withdraw nuclear weapons from Belarus and drop plans for intermediate-range missiles there. [41] 444 also carried the Finland demand. [42] It is a press report of an unofficial paper, not a Russian state statement. [41]
countries.sw: Host-nation support: Baltic basing limits and a Belarus missile pledge would touch the eastern-flank posture JFC Brunssum plans for, so the terms are a planning input even before any official text.

q.en: it would block further NATO enlargement

items.h: UK buys three mine-hunting drone motherships under a Norway deal
items.body: UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and Norway's Tore O. Sandvik finalised the purchase on 12 Nov at the Atlantic Future Forum in Oslo, with £90 million ($119.1 million) allocated under the Lunna House Agreement. [43] The ships follow Norway's P1118 vessel design, the first is due in 2031 and the UK holds an option for three more. [43] The UK says they support anti-submarine warfare on NATO's northern flank. [43]
items.sw: Autonomous mine countermeasures on the northern flank enter the sea-lane assumptions that reinforcement planning across Allied Command Operations relies on.

items.h: Italy raises GCAP fighter spending and cuts army vehicle funding
items.body: Italy's 2026 defence budget documents show GCAP spending of €875 million, up from €625 million in 2025 and well above the €275 million planned. [44] Spending on new Rheinmetall-based tanks and fighting vehicles plus Ariete upgrades fell to €177 million from €281 million, against a €425 million forecast; the 2027 forecast is €872 million. [44] The 1,050 Lynx and 272 Panther deal is worth about €23 billion. [44]
items.sw: Slower Italian land-vehicle delivery affects the land-force capability targets NATO defence planning assigns to Italy.

items.h: US bases in England go to FPCON Charlie over an Iranian threat, the WSJ reports
items.body: The War Zone reported on 13 Nov that security levels were raised at US bases in England and that KC-135 tankers left RAF Mildenhall from 9 Nov; citing the Wall Street Journal, it put Mildenhall and Lakenheath at Force Protection Condition (FPCON) Charlie over an Iranian threat. [34] The same evening US Air Force Security Forces responded to suspected drones over Lakenheath. [34] Neither the Pentagon nor the UK Ministry of Defence has published the threat. [34]
items.sw: Posture: FPCON Charlie at the main US tanker and fighter bases in Britain shows how an Iran contingency now reaches into the European rear area that NATO reinforcement plans count on.

items.h: Ukraine-founded UFORCE raises $700 million at a $6 billion valuation
items.body: Defense One reported on 13 Nov that drone maker UFORCE raised a $700 million Series A led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK National Wealth Fund, with the US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund also investing. [45] Revenue doubled and headcount tripled to over 1,000; the company claims its Nemesis drone has destroyed over 10,000 Russian vehicles, a figure not independently verified. [45] It plans more unmanned surface vessels, ground and air integration, and acquisitions. [45]
items.sw: Western capital now backs Ukrainian-origin drone makers directly, which shapes the supplier base for NATO-interoperable systems.

items.h: Beretta shows an eight-shotgun remote turret for last-line drone defence
items.body: The War Zone reported on 13 Nov that Beretta's LIVET remote weapon station pairs eight Benelli M4 shotguns with AI-assisted tracking as a short-range, last-line defence against small drones. [46]
items.sw: It is a cheap inner layer for the point defence of command posts and bases under NATO counter-drone planning.

items.h: Hermeus brings Northrop Grumman onto the Quarterhorse drone
items.body: Hermeus announced on 13 Nov that Northrop Grumman will supply Quarterhorse mission systems (electronic warfare, communications, sensing, navigation), with trials of the Northrop kit expected in the summer. [47] The Defense Innovation Unit funds the drone, Anduril supplies autonomy software and Hermeus will build the Pratt & Whitney F100 engine under licence, aiming for speeds up to Mach 3. [47]
items.sw: Autonomous high-speed reconnaissance aircraft would feed the same joint targeting picture NATO commands draw on.

ttp.title: Week in war, 8–14 Nov: base drones, layered counter-drone kit and robots in the assault
body: The clearest pattern of the week is the layering of defence against small drones. On 13 Nov The War Zone reported Beretta's LIVET remote weapon station, which puts eight Benelli M4 shotguns on a turret with AI-assisted tracking as a short-range, last-line defence. [46] The same day Defense News showed Motorola Solutions' EAGLS air defence platform and a planned successor, built around affordable, modular counter-drone kit. [48] At doctrine level, the US Air Force's classified Force Design 2026, announced on 13 Nov, moves away from intercepting individual drones toward sensors and software, and calls for autonomy and command and control linked to aircraft in denied environments. [49]

Drones over bases are the second pattern. On 13 Nov US Air Force Security Forces responded to suspected unauthorised drones over RAF Lakenheath; no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected, and bases in England had raised security levels earlier in the week, The War Zone reported. [34]

On the ground in Ukraine, ground robots are now part of the assault rather than only the supply line. EUobserver's battlefield update of 6 Nov said Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps sent dozens of robots into one assault; a Russian channel counted two carrying Mk 19 grenade launchers, 18 carrying two RPGs each and eight kamikaze robots, and the outcome rests on Russian sources only. [50] The same update said shoot-down rates against drones are improving only slowly. [50]

Production follows the money: UFORCE raised $700 million on 13 Nov to scale its drones and surface vessels, and says its Nemesis drone has destroyed over 10,000 Russian vehicles, a company claim. [45]

items.h: llama.cpp reaches v1.0.0 with a stable C API and semantic versioning
items.body: The ggml-org project released llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0 on 13 Nov, about 3.5 years after the project began. It covers more than 150 model architecture variants and all mainstream speculative decoding methods, and ships builds for Linux, macOS, Windows, Android and iOS [51]. Breaking API or ABI changes now require a major-version bump [51].
items.sw: A stable, versioned local inference library lets a staff section pin a tested build and run models offline on disconnected or classified laptops without surprise API breaks.

items.h: IBM releases Granite 4.1 LLMON previews that separate instructions from data
items.body: IBM published two experimental preview models, granite-4.1-3b-llmon-preview and granite-4.1-8b-llmon-preview, on 12 Nov. LLMON marks structure with reserved special tokens, so instructions and data sit apart [52]. IBM says the models avoid 47% more prompt-injection attacks than the best frontier model it tested and 95% more than the best open-source model on the OPI benchmark, with general capability on par with Granite 4.1 Instruct. These are vendor figures and the models are not for production [52].
items.sw: Prompt injection through ingested documents is the main risk when an assistant summarises open-source or partner reporting, and token-level separation of data from instructions is a mitigation staff can test before any pilot.

items.h: Researcher finds Blackwell fingerprints in leading Chinese open-weight models
items.body: Will DePue of Unemployment Labs analysed released weights and reports that Moonshot's Kimi K3 and DeepSeek's V4 carry signs of training on Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, which are banned from export to China [53]. Epoch AI estimates about 2 million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through concealment schemes, and 275,000 Nvidia accelerators went to Malaysia [53]. The finding does not prove violations, since the chips could sit in offshore data centres [53].
items.sw: Export-control evasion through third-country data centres affects how allies assess adversary AI capability, so this feeds technology-transfer and capability-assessment inputs to NATO threat estimates.

cards.n: The Senate agreed to vote on H.Con.Res. 93, the Iran war-powers resolution, no later than 20 Nov.
The continuing resolution at FY2026 levels runs out; no new starts until then.
White House call on a permanent US presence in Poland that the Pentagon has backed.
Target date to stand up the four-star Autonomous Warfare Command; it needs congressional authorisation and no commander is named. [54]

dod.h: Pentagon renames its AI office the Super Intelligence Office
dod.body: On 13 Nov the Defense Department redesignated the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office as the Super Intelligence Office, led by Cameron Stanley, following a September order from President Trump to say “super intelligence” across government. [55] The office runs the Maven Smart System, the War Data Platform (formerly Advana) and GenAI.mil, and the department says existing programmes and solicitations continue uninterrupted. [55] The rebrand rolls out over the coming weeks under a new SI.mil site. [55]
dod.sw: Maven Smart System and GenAI.mil are the tools US counterparts use alongside NATO staffs, so contract and portal names on US-side data requests will change.
dod.fy: Expect SI.mil and new office names on US data-sharing requests in the coming weeks.

dod.h: Air Force adopts a classified Force Design 2026 built on sensors and autonomy
dod.body: The Air Force announced Force Design 2026 on 13 Nov, replacing the October 2024 One Force Design; the document is classified with no releasable copy. [49] It shifts counter-drone work from intercepting single drones toward sensors and software, and calls for autonomy, sensors and command and control integrated with aircraft in denied environments. [49] Chief of Staff Gen. Ken Wilsbach said it “presents a fundamental shift”. [49]
dod.sw: The sensor-and-software approach to air defence will shape the joint track and targeting data the Army contributes to NATO integrated air and missile defence.

news.h: Army names the lieutenant colonel held in the UK over alleged help to Russian intelligence
news.body: Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner, 41, an Army human resources officer, was arrested earlier this week under sections 1 and 3 of Britain's National Security Act 2023, Defense News reported on 13 Nov. [15] He was assigned at Imjin Barracks, Gloucestershire, home of NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, and remains in custody in London; Counter Terrorism Policing London leads the case and no charge has been reported. [15] Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commanding Army Counterintelligence Command, called insider threats “real and persistent” and asked personnel to report suspicious activity to their local counterintelligence office. [15]
news.sw: He held a field-grade post in a NATO headquarters, so the case falls under the same Army counterintelligence reporting requirement (AR 381-12) that covers every US officer in a NATO billet, Brunssum included.
news.fy: Check you know your local counterintelligence office contact and the date of your next threat-awareness briefing.

career.note: Nothing new for a field-grade officer in a NATO billet in the window; see the Tyner case under Army news for the counterintelligence reporting reminder.

research.title: Combat Power, Sustained: A Hub-and-Mesh Architecture for Contested Logistics
summary: Andrews, a US Air Force weapons officer who leads global mobility operations at the 618th Air Operations Center, argues that the services' dispersal concepts (agile combat employment, distributed maritime operations, expeditionary advanced base operations and multidomain operations) complicate the enemy's targeting but raise the logistics burden. [56] The theatre must be set while major combat is under way, so the network is still being built while it is under attack. [56]

He sees two failure modes. Concentrating capacity in a few hubs makes those hubs targets; spreading it everywhere leaves each site too thinly protected. [56] His answer is a hub-and-mesh architecture: keep the major gateways, add alternate airfields and routes, and make sure that losing one hub does not stop combat power from flowing. [56] A mesh must do more than offer other landing sites: diverted cargo must still reach the supported force in time for the commander's manoeuvre plan. [56]

He draws on history and current practice. About 85% of US combat power is based in the continental United States, so homeland mobility infrastructure is itself a target. [56] In Operation Nickel Grass (1973), 22,305 tons moved in 32 days on 566 C-5 and C-141 missions, and European landing and overflight denials made Lajes Field in the Azores critical. [56] He quotes a Ukrainian commander's rule, “You never take off and land in the same airfield,” and Gen. James Hecker's remark that defenders “can only protect a few” airfields. [56] The article is a serving officer's argument and states that it does not reflect official positions. [56]
findings: About 85% of US combat power is based in the continental United States. [56]
Operation Nickel Grass (1973): 22,305 tons over 32 days on 566 C-5 and C-141 missions, with European denials making Lajes Field critical. [56]
Tarawa: engineers returned a shell-damaged airfield to operation within 15 hours. [56]
Proposal: set up alternate aerial ports connected to working theatre distribution paths before disruption, and define how much displaced demand each can absorb. [56]
Proposal: assign clear authority to redirect flow between USTRANSCOM (strategic mobility) and the geographic combatant command (theatre distribution). [56]
Proposal: track cargo contents, recipients and timing, not just aircraft location. [56]
research.method: Argument by historical case (Nickel Grass, Tarawa, the Red Ball Express, Operation Iraqi Freedom) and current Ukrainian practice; no model, wargame or dataset. It cannot show that a mesh would hold under a modern strike campaign, or what it would cost.
research.sw: For Brunssum: the same logic applies to reception, staging and onward movement across Europe, where alternate airfields, rail and road links and the authority to redirect flow between strategic and theatre commands need settling before a crisis, not during it.

research.title: A natural field experiment on the effectiveness of economic sanctions before and after the Russian invasion of Ukraine
research.authors: Michael G. Findley, Daniel L. Nielson, J. C. Sharman
summary: The authors tested whether sanctioned Russian officials could still reach the international financial system. They emailed 7,081 solicitations to corporate service providers (law firms and incorporation services that form shell companies and open accounts) in 202 countries and jurisdictions, using the names of six Russian officials on Magnitsky sanctions lists with altered middle initials, and compared the replies with those to placebo names. [57] Two rounds were run, one before the February 2022 invasion and one in May 2022. [57]

Before the invasion, sanctioned names did not fare significantly worse than placebo names. After it, they did: replies fell, and non-compliant offers declined. [57] The authors conclude that war-related factors, not sanctions law itself, were decisive, because the legal regime was the same in both rounds. [57] Sanctioned names still received many positive responses, so access was reduced, not closed: of 76 firms taken to the payment stage, 15 completed an incorporation, and no firm materially changed its compliance requirements. [57]
findings: 7,081 emails to firms in 202 jurisdictions; 5,084 firms in the final sample. [57]
Pre-invasion round (Magnitsky-law countries, n = 1,502): non-compliant responses 4.6% for sanctioned names against 2.4% for placebo; P = 0.104, not significant. [57]
Post-invasion round (n = 715): no reply 89.5% for sanctioned names against 78.8% for placebo; P = 0.0001. [57]
Post-invasion drop in the non-compliant response rate: 4.0 percentage points (95% CI 1.2 to 6.8, P = 0.006). [57]
15 of 76 firms followed to payment completed an incorporation; none materially changed requirements. [57]
research.method: Preregistered audit-style field experiment with random assignment within blocks and two independent coders; 3,484 hybrid observations (33%) excluded. Banks were not contacted, only corporate service providers, and the study measures access to company formation and accounts, not the wider economic effect of sanctions on Russia.
research.sw: Enforcement by private intermediaries, not the sanctions lists alone, decides whether sanctions bite, and many of those intermediaries sit in European jurisdictions.

research.title: The Impact of Climate Change on Fisheries (NBER Working Paper 35994)
research.authors: Fabio Cevenini, Christopher Costello, Carlo Fezzi
summary: The authors give what they call the first causal estimate of how ocean temperature variation affects fishing revenue, using 2.5 million spatially explicit revenue observations from all European fishing vessels for 2013 to 2022. [58] The key variable, “Marine Degree Days”, measures a species' exposure to temperatures relative to its biologically established thermal tolerance range. [58]

Deviations from species' thermal preferences cause significant revenue losses, and heat exposure has the largest effect; vertical mobility and ecological traits mediate it. [58] Under climate scenarios, revenue declines are widespread by 2100, reaching €560 million a year in the warmest scenario, with lower-income equatorial areas hit hardest and some colder regions gaining. [58] Only the abstract page was read; the coefficients are in the paper. [58]
findings: 2.5 million spatially explicit revenue observations, all European fishing vessels, 2013 to 2022. [58]
Heat exposure beyond species' thermal tolerance has the largest negative effect on revenue. [58]
Projected loss of up to €560 million a year by 2100 in the warmest scenario. [58]
Losses are largest in lower-income equatorial areas; some colder regions gain. [58]
research.method: Panel estimation of revenue on a species-specific temperature exposure index, with controls for spatial selection and ecological interdependence, then projection under several climate scenarios. The projections depend on scenario assumptions and cannot show how fleets or prices would adapt.
research.sw: It puts a euro figure on warming for Europe's own fishing fleets, the first sector to feel it in coastal economies.

philosophy.quote: In these matters the same principle of preference that applies to the parts of the soul must apply also to the activities of those parts: war must be for the sake of peace, business for the sake of leisure, things necessary and useful for the purpose of things noble.
philosophy.translation: H. Rackham, Aristotle: Politics, Loeb Classical Library (Harvard University Press, 1944), as given on Perseus.
philosophy.gloss: Aristotle has just divided the soul into a part that has reason and a part that obeys it, and split the rational part into practical and theoretical reason. He argues that the same ranking holds for activities: the lower exists for the sake of the higher, so war exists for peace, as work exists for leisure. [59] The sentence sits in the ideal-state books, where he asks what the lawgiver should educate citizens for, and its use is polemical: in the same chapter he faults lawgivers who admire Sparta's constitution for training citizens only to conquer, a state safe only while it fights. The strongest challenge comes from the rival view Aristotle is writing against, put most sharply in Heraclitus' fragment that war is “father of all and king of all” (DK 22 B53): if war generates the order it is said to serve, it cannot be ranked simply as a means to peace.

redteam.title: The week no one had to claim
redteam.premise: Allies assume the November hoax bomb threats, supermarket cold-chain cyberattacks and rail sabotage are a nuisance each nation can absorb through its own police and national CERT, without a shared attribution.
body: Our staff measures a week by the form of the reply, not by damage. Gerasimov wrote in 2013 that “The role of non-military means of achieving political and strategic goals has grown, and, in many cases, they have exceeded the power of force of weapons in their effectiveness.” [60] Nothing in the week of 8 to 14 November was kinetic, and nothing needed to be. The allied assumption under test is that this is acceptable: each capital files the incidents with its police and its CERT and moves on.

Read the replies as we would. France named an IRGC unit for its October fridge attacks on 9 November and the Paris prosecutor sought international arrest warrants. [61] Belgium split in public three days later: Interior Minister Quintin pointed to Iran, and Foreign Minister Prévot called that “trop précoce” (“too early”). [62] Paris prosecutors opened a separate inquiry on 7 November into the hoax emails and “any potential links they may have to foreign powers”. [63] That is three files in two countries with three different answers, while more than 100 stores had already been hit. [64] The EU agriculture commissioner called it a deliberate attempt to disrupt the food supply, and that is a statement, not a joint finding. [65]

Our objective is not credit. It is to keep the target society busy with itself. The 2014 Military Doctrine lists use of “the protest potential of the population” among the features of modern conflict, and Gerasimov described non-military measures “applied in coordination with the protest potential of the population”, aimed “to create a permanently operating front through the entire territory of the enemy state”. [60, 66] A hoax email costs the sender almost nothing and costs the state a school day: 6,300 Italian schools on 11 November and more than 3,700 on 12 November, the day the Taoiseach named hoaxes among the attacks on Europe at the Dublin summit. [67] The front runs through classrooms, check-in halls and cold rooms, not through a border.

The attribution split is where the week paid. Where a capital names Iran, the cold-chain file becomes an Iranian file in a separate theatre, and the hoax file stays unnamed. Where a capital names no one, the CERT closes the ticket. An outside analyst wrote on 10 November that these attacks are hard to attribute and that Moscow is likely to intensify them. [68] Our constraints point the same way: deniability, low cost per event, and no single act that forces a collective decision. A shared attribution is the one outcome that would convert thirty national nuisances into one alliance problem, so our planning treats the national reflex as the protected asset.

What would show our week was wasted is observable: a joint finding or a common sanctions listing that covers hoaxes, cold chain and rail together, rather than one capital naming one actor for one file.
assumptions: national police and CERTs are enough
attribution can stay national and slow
each file can be handled alone

items.h: Coalition talks move to De Zwaluwenberg after eight hours end without a deal
items.body: Prime Minister Rob Jetten (D66), VVD leader Dilan Yeşilgöz and CDA deputy prime minister Van den Brink talked for more than eight hours at the Ministry of General Affairs on 13 Nov without settling the coalition crisis. [19] Jetten said: “Ons werk is nog lang niet klaar” (“Our work is far from finished”); Yeşilgöz called the minority cabinet a “mislukt experiment” (“failed experiment”) and asked that D66 and CDA stop doing deals with the left, possibly with another right-wing party in the cabinet. [5, 19] The six party leaders and parliamentary chairs resume today at the De Zwaluwenberg estate; Yeşilgöz said one outcome could be that the three go to the King. [5, 19]
items.sw: Host-nation support: a caretaker Dutch cabinet could not take new decisions on defence spending or host-nation arrangements for JFC Brunssum until a new coalition forms.

items.h: US air traffic halt delays Schiphol's flights to the United States
items.body: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) halted all air traffic in the United States for about five hours from about 22:00 Dutch time on 13 Nov after communications equipment at regional air-traffic-control centres was overloaded, the longest nationwide stop in 25 years. [35] Eurocontrol suspended flights from its 42 member states, the Netherlands among them, to the US at the FAA's request, and Schiphol said US departures were delayed by a few hours. [35] The FAA reopened the airspace at about 03:00, and NOS reported that normal traffic could take days to return. [35]
items.sw: Civil transportation, baseline requirement 7: a single US system fault grounded transatlantic flights from 42 European states, the corridor US reinforcement and leave travel both use.
items.fy: Check your airline app before any US-bound trip this weekend; the December flight to New York is not affected yet.
